news.title: ‘Terrible mistake’: Trump backs Infantino after explosive letter revealed
news.lede: Updated August 11, 2026 - 4.53am. First published August 10, 2026 - 10.05pm. Long-time supporter of Gianni Infantino, US President Donald Trump has explosively backed the FIFA president, posting on his Truth Social account that the federation would “be making a terrible mistake” if they replaced him. The post came after the European football’s governing body UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF issued an open letter attacking the FIFA chief’s conduct during the proposed sale of a stake in World Cup commercial rights.

news.title: Trump jumps to Infantino’s defence as Fifa split widens, rival tourneys planned
news.lede: US President Donald Trump has leapt to the defence of embattled Fifa chief Gianni Infantino, saying it would be “a terrible mistake” if football got rid of the head of the game’s world governing body. Nearly two weeks after Infantino’s plan to sell off the World Cup was leaked, Trump finally had his say in an early Tuesday post on his social media site Truth Social. Trump, who was awarded the first Fifa Peace Prize by Infantino before this year’s World Cup, warned that removing the 56-year-old Swiss lawyer would be a costly move. “Fifa would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino,” Trump wrote.

news.title: UEFA, AFC, CONCACAF renew attacks on Infantino over failed stake sale
news.lede: Three of FIFA’s six confederations issued an open letter to the “football family” on Monday attacking President Gianni Infantino‘s conduct during the proposed sale of a stake in World Cup commercial rights and calling for leadership that works for the game. The letter, co-signed by the presidents of UEFA, AFC and CONCACAF, called for an independent review of the now-abandoned proposaland said Infantino had broken trust “through deception” and “placed himself above the collective”. “Football’s strength has always been its unity,” it read. “We call for that unity to be honoured now, for leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it.”

news.title: World football bodies accuse FIFA of 'deception' in World Cup plans
news.lede: Football powerbrokers in Europe, North America and Asia believe FIFA president Gianni Infantino's recent plan to sell an interest in the World Cup was a “fundamental breach of trust” with the institutions that the sport's global governing body serves. In an “open letter to the football family” revealed on Monday (local time), UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC also said that “when trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned”. UEFA runs football in Europe, CONCACAF is the confederation for North and Central America and the Caribbean, and the AFC governs the sport in Asia. The letter was co-signed by UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin, AFC president Salman Bin Ibrahim Al-Khalifa, CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani and the general secretaries of those continental governing bodies.

news.title: Donald Trump says it would be a ‘terrible mistake’ to replace Fifa’s Gianni Infantino
news.lede: US president backs ‘fantastic’ Infantino in Truth Social post. Infantino under pressure following doomed World Cup sell-off plan. US president Donald Trump has warned Fifa would be making a “terrible mistake” if they get rid of Gianni Infantino as the head of world football’s governing body. Infantino has come under pressure following his doomed plan to sell off stakes in the men’s World Cup to private investors.

news.title: How Gianni Infantino's FIFA leadership imploded over two weeks
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has been embroiled in a scandal that has endured for more than two weeks. (Reuters: Dylan Martinez). After weeks of pressure, three of the world's largest continental football confederations have issued a joint open letter attacking the leadership of FIFA President Gianni Infantino over his failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup. The presidents and general secretaries of the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA), Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF) said the saga showed Mr Infantino "places himself above the collection that entrusted him with authority".

news.title: [Official] 'Challenging for Back-to-Back Round of 16' U20 Women's World Cup Final Roster Announced
news.lede: The roster for the South Korean U20 women's national football team competing in the 2026 FIFA U20 Women's World Cup has been announced. The Korea Football Association (KFA) revealed the final 21-player roster to participate in the 2026 FIFA U20 Women's World Cup, which will be held in Poland this September. The head coach is Park Yoon-jeong. The U20 Yeo Ja (CEO) team secured qualification for the World Cup finals by reaching the semifinals of the AFC U20 Women's Asian Cup held in Bangkok, Thailand, last April.
